{"entries":[{"name":"Ｋ","reading":"ケー","category":"character","keys":["Ｋ"],"content":"A close childhood friend of the narrator, who is referred to only by the letter K. He was the second son of a Buddhist priest in the same home region as the narrator, and was adopted into a wealthy doctor's family, which funded his move to Tokyo to study. In Tokyo he boarded in the same lodging house as the narrator, and the two shared a room. The narrator describes him as strong-willed and serious, and says that he constantly used the word 精進 (shōjin) and that his conduct seemed to the narrator to be summed up by that word. The narrator secretly held K in deep reverence, and the two young men, though fearful of Tokyo and its people, talked of becoming great men."},{"name":"精進","reading":"しょうじん","category":"term","keys":["精進"],"content":"A Buddhist term meaning single-minded devotion and diligent effort, often associated with ascetic practice.
